summary: Re-stamp organization-wide UPLOAD rows to their uploader (owner ruling 2026-07-20 'no backward compatibility'; epic cinatra#1883 C3, issue #1887). Before slice C1 (#1885/#1916, merged) every upload was written organization-wide; C1 cut new upload writes to uploader-owned (owner_level='user', owner_id=<uploader>, visibility='private'). This ONE-SHOT backfill re-derives the historical rows to match. TARGET: objects where data->>'originKind'='upload' AND visibility='organization' (the exact signal the canonical read filter's organization clause keys on — src/lib/derived-store-ownership.ts) AND created_by IS NOT NULL, EXCLUDING rows deliberately widened to org through the approvals flow (a durable artifact_promotion_request row with status='approved' AND to_visibility='organization' — the only signal distinguishing a deliberate share from a legacy default, since a promotion must WIDEN so a legacy already-org upload can never carry one). RE-DERIVE: owner_level→'user', owner_id→created_by, visibility→'private'; project_id KEPT (refinement survives). Non-upload origins and already-promoted rows are NEVER touched. IDEMPOTENT: a re-stamped row reads visibility='private' so the UPDATE matches zero rows on re-run; a fresh bootstrap has no legacy org uploads (no-op, ledger-faked). FAIL-LOUD: node-pg-migrate wraps the queued steps in one transaction (any error rolls the whole migration back — no partial apply) and a postcondition DO block RAISEs if any upload-origin org-visible non-promoted row survives (the only survivor is a NULL-created_by anomaly with no uploader to re-derive to). DOWN throws (irreversible: a privatized row is indistinguishable from a natively-private C1 upload, so a faithful reverse cannot exist — same class as core__0033; restore from backup). SEQ PROVISIONAL: renumbered at merge if a lower free seq opens (core__0063 is claimed by PR #1915; rename-only, zero SQL change). ROLLOUT / OPERATOR NOTE: this is a VISIBILITY-NARROWING data change — after it applies, historical org-wide uploads are visible only to their uploader; users who need one shared again use the /artifacts promotion flow (#1437). An org announcement accompanies the release per the epic ruling. SPOT-CHECK (run in the app schema before/after): pre-count = SELECT count(*) FROM objects WHERE data->>'originKind'='upload' AND visibility='organization'; post-condition = the same query returns only explicitly-org-promoted ids (0 for a store with no org promotions); verify a promoted upload (approved org artifact_promotion_request) still reads visibility='organization', a non-upload org row is untouched, and a re-stamped row reads owner_level='user'/owner_id=created_by/visibility='private' with project_id preserved.
